base_cards.front: Complete: une fille sportif___.
back: sportive.

base_cards.front: Complete: nous ___ français (parler, present).
back: parlons.

base_cards.front: Translate: je voudrais.
back: I would like.

base_cards.front: Translate: ne...plus.
back: No longer / not anymore.

base_cards.front: Complete: à + les = ___.
back: aux.

base_cards.front: Complete: de + le = ___.
back: du.

base_cards.front: Translate: je viens de finir.
back: I have just finished.

base_cards.front: Give the past participle of faire.
back: fait.

base_cards.front: Give the present nous form of choisir.
back: choisissons.

base_cards.front: Translate: mieux.
back: Better (as an adverb).

base_cards.front: Correct: Elle est allé. Ils mange. (perfect then present)
back: Elle est **allée**.
Ils **mangent**.

base_cards.front: Translate: Je n'ai pas encore mangé.
back: I have not eaten yet.
The negative is **not yet**, not never.

base_cards.front: Explain the difference between je jouais and j'ai joué.
back: Je jouais: I used to play / was playing; past habit or background.
J'ai joué: I played / have played; completed action.

base_cards.front: Replace les livres with a pronoun: Je regarde les livres.
back: Je **les** regarde.
Les is a direct object pronoun and goes before regarde.

base_cards.front: Replace à mes amis with a pronoun: Je parle à mes amis.
back: Je **leur** parle.
Parler à takes an indirect object; leur here means to them.

base_cards.front: Translate: Je n'ai que deux livres.
back: I only have two books.
**Ne...que** means only.

base_cards.front: Why is son used in son amie when the friend is female?
back: The possessive is before a vowel, so **son** replaces sa. It can mean his friend or her friend.

base_cards.front: Translate: J'habite ici depuis trois ans.
back: I have lived here for three years.
The present with depuis describes something still continuing.

base_cards.front: Turn tu regardes into a command, then give the vous command.
back: Regarde ! Regardez !
The regular -er tu command drops -s; vous keeps -ez.

base_cards.front: Give the feminine and masculine plural of heureux.
back: Heureuse; heureux.
The masculine plural already ends in -x.

base_cards.front: Translate: We are going to visit a town that is very beautiful.
back: Nous allons visiter une ville qui est très belle.
**Allons + infinitive**; qui is the relative subject; belle agrees with ville.

base_cards.front: Translate: After eating, I watched a film.
back: Après avoir mangé, j'ai regardé un film.
Use **après avoir + participle**, then the perfect.

base_cards.front: Translate: Nobody comes because there are no buses.
back: Personne ne vient parce qu'il n'y a pas de bus.
Personne is the subject; a negative quantity uses de.

base_cards.front: Translate: This letter is written by my sister.
back: Cette lettre est écrite par ma sœur.
Present **passive**, with écrite agreeing with lettre.

base_cards.front: Translate: I want some, but I am not going there.
back: J'en veux, mais je n'y vais pas.
En replaces the quantity; y replaces the place.

base_cards.front: Correct: Elles est gentil. Je veux regarde le film. J'ai quinze années.
back: Elles **sont gentilles**. Je veux **regarder** le film. J'ai quinze **ans**.
Check subject/adjective agreement, the infinitive after a modal and the age expression.

base_cards.front: Translate: Next year, I will work in France. I would like to help people because it is important.
back: L'année prochaine, je travaillerai en France. Je voudrais aider les gens parce que c'est important.
Travaillerai uses the regular future; voudrais aider expresses a wish; en fits France; the final clause supplies a reason.

base_cards.front: Explain the grammar in: Les photos que j'ai prises sont belles.
back: Photos is feminine plural.
Que is the relative direct object of ai prises.
The direct object comes before the avoir perfect, so prises agrees with photos.
Sont and belles agree with the plural subject.

updates.front: Give the feminine and masculine plural of heureux.
back: Feminine singular: heureuse. Feminine plural: heureuses. Masculine plural: heureux.
The masculine form already ends in -x, so it does not add another plural ending.

additions.front: Translate: It was raining when we arrived.
back: Il pleuvait quand nous sommes arrivés.
Write arrivées for an all-female group.

additions.front: Why can “Il pleuvait” and “nous sommes arrivés” occur together?
back: The imperfect gives the ongoing background. The perfect gives a completed event within it.

additions.front: Translate: I was watching a film when my brother came in.
back: Je regardais un film quand mon frère est entré.

additions.front: How do “nous jouerons” and “nous jouerions” differ?
back: Nous jouerons means we will play. Nous jouerions means we would play.

additions.front: Correct: J’ai allé au parc.
back: Je suis allé(e) au parc.
Aller uses être in this construction; its participle agrees with the subject.

additions.front: Do all movement verbs use être in the perfect tense?
back: No. Marcher and voyager, for example, use avoir: j’ai marché; j’ai voyagé. Learn the particular auxiliary.

additions.front: Replace le musée: Je vais visiter le musée.
back: Je vais le visiter.

additions.front: Make “Je les regarde” negative.
back: Je ne les regarde pas.

additions.front: Why is qui used in “une amie qui travaille”?
back: Qui replaces the subject of travaille: the friend does the action.

additions.front: Why is que used in “le livre que je lis”?
back: Je is the subject of lis. Que replaces its direct object, the book.

additions.front: Replace the place: Je vais à Paris.
back: J’y vais.

additions.front: Replace des pommes while preserving the number: Je veux deux pommes.
back: J’en veux deux.

additions.front: Translate: I am not going to work.
back: Je ne vais pas travailler.

additions.front: Translate: I did not work.
back: Je n’ai pas travaillé.

additions.front: Translate: I only have one brother.
back: Je n’ai qu’un frère.

additions.front: Translate: I no longer play football.
back: Je ne joue plus au football.

additions.front: How do you build the regular -er conditional?
back: Add the imperfect endings to the infinitive, for example parler + ais gives je parlerais.

additions.front: Translate: The book is written by a journalist.
back: Le livre est écrit par un journaliste.
Une journaliste is correct for a female journalist.

additions.front: Translate: Nobody comes.
back: Personne ne vient.

additions.front: Translate: I have just finished.
back: Je viens de finir.

additions.front: Why does “J’habite ici depuis deux ans” use the present?
back: The action began earlier and still continues: I have lived here for two years.

additions.front: Translate: After eating, I am going to work.
back: Après avoir mangé, je vais travailler.
